newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's NLB bank launches five-year bond.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's NLB bank launches five-year bond.

text.p: State-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka, Slovenia's largest bank, said on Monday it had launched a five-year bond in the value of $27 million.
The issue has two tranches. One is denominated in tolars with a total value of 2.37 billion tolars, while the other is denominated in German marks with a value of 20 million marks.
The tolar issue will pay interest of 6.75 percent over Slovenia's basic interest rate TOM, while the mark issue will carry an interest rate of seven percent.
TOM, which changes monthly according to the rate of inflation over the past 12 months, amounted to a monthly rate of 0.7 percent in May.

The public tender for the bond lasts to September 1. The bank said it would ask the Ljubljana bourse to list the bond immediately after the tender closes. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
